title: InfinityStar: Uniﬁed Spacetime AutoRegressive Modeling for Visual Generatio

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (2) claims to be the autoregressive likelihood for the whole video, but each factor is written as p(r_k^c | r_1^c, ..., r_{k-1}^c, psi(t)), with no conditioning on any tokens from clips 1,...,c-1. The displayed factorization therefore makes separate clips conditionally independent given the text, contradicting the immediately preceding statement that clips are generated sequentially conditioned on prior clips and Section 3.4's attention to the preceding clip. The condition must include prior-clip token blocks (or an explicit compressed history representation).

The method states that the first K_s scale tuples are repeated 'N times.' However, N was explicitly defined in Section 3.2 as the number of sequential clips in a video. The implementation instead says that the first 7 scales are repeated 6 times. Thus the repetition count is both undefined as a separate hyperparameter and inconsistent with the established meaning of N; under the stated notation it would vary with the number of clips rather than be fixed at six.

Table 2 attributes the VideoCrafter-2.0 result to reference [5], but reference [5] is explicitly titled 'VideoCrafter1: Open diffusion models for high-quality video generation.' VideoCrafter-2.0 is a different work/version, so this citation does not identify the reported baseline correctly.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction and Section 4.3, citation of VBench as [38]
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly identifies [38] as the VBench benchmark, but bibliography entry [38] is titled 'Evaluation Agent: Efficient and Promptable Evaluation Framework for Visual Generative Models.' It is not the standard VBench benchmark citation, whose bibliographic record should be supplied if VBench scores are being reported. The cited reference/title does not substantiate the stated benchmark attribution.

The table reports 354 s for Nova and 58 s for InfinityStar, while defining Wan's 1864 s result as 1x. Relative to InfinityStar, Nova's speedup is 354/58 = 6.10x, not the reported 5x. This also conflicts with the surrounding text, which correctly states that InfinityStar is approximately 6x faster than Nova.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.4, Spacetime Sparse Attention discussion versus Table 5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says SSA 'reaches 1.5× speedup when generating 192p 16f' and later describes 1.1x and 1.5x speedups for '192p and 480p 16f.' Table 5 contains no 16-frame condition: it reports 192p at 65 and 161 frames and 480p at 161 frames. The approximately 1.5x value occurs for 192p/161 frames (24.3/16.7), whereas 192p/65 frames yields only about 1.12x (8.6/7.7). Moreover, the 480p full-attention comparison is OOM, so Table 5 cannot support a 480p speedup against full attention.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction and Section 4.3 claim that InfinityStar surpasses HunyuanVideo / establishes state of the art among autoregressive models
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claimed 83.74 VBench score is explicitly marked as using prompt rewriting. The text simultaneously acknowledges that baselines use 'variable' prompt enhancements, while Table 2 does not mark HunyuanVideo as using the same rewriting protocol. A score produced under a materially different prompt-processing procedure is not a controlled head-to-head comparison. Consequently, the reported table may be descriptive, but it does not by itself support the comparative claim that InfinityStar surpasses HunyuanVideo or establishes a benchmark ranking without matched prompting and evaluation settings.
